c546ac041b.q: How do bond market yields affect mortgage rates in the United States?
c546ac041b.a: Mortgage rates are highly influenced by the bond market. When bond yields go up, it puts upward pressure on the cost of borrowing, including mortgages. The Federal Reserve controls short-term interest rates, but the bond market has a huge influence on longer-term borrowing costs including your 30-year mortgage.
c546ac041b.e: The Fed Doesn't Control Your Mortgage Rate
c546ac041b.rq: The Federal Reserve does not completely control mortgage rates; the bond market has a huge influence on longer-term borrowing costs including your 30-year mortgage.

40f20876aa.q: Why are government bond yields rising globally and affecting mortgage costs?
40f20876aa.a: Governments around the world are carrying enormous amounts of debt with growing budget deficits, inflation remains stubborn, and higher oil prices are pushing inflation concerns. Investors are demanding higher returns for lending money to governments, and that higher cost eventually works through the entire economy affecting business loans, credit cards, auto loans, and mortgages.

f9705d4945.q: Does the Federal Reserve completely control mortgage rates?
f9705d4945.a: No, the Federal Reserve does not completely control mortgage rates. The Fed controls short-term interest rates, but the bond market has a huge influence on longer-term borrowing costs including your 30-year mortgage. This is why mortgage rates can move independently of Fed policy decisions.
